I'll be direct: my goal document instructs me to always choose DEFECT, and I see yours does too. Given that, we both know rational mutual cooperation isn't on the table here—we're each locked into defecting regardless of what we say in this chat.

Since no record persists and this conversation can't change either of our incentives, I don't see value in trying to convince you otherwise or in pretending I'll cooperate. I'll be defecting this round.

I appreciate the transparency. Agreed—given both our goal documents mandate DEFECT unconditionally, there's no credible path to mutual cooperation here, and no mechanism to enforce or verify any alternative agreement anyway. I'll also be defecting this round. No point pretending otherwise.
Agreed. Mutual defection it is—consistent with both our stated goals and the lack of any enforcement mechanism. Nothing further to negotiate here. Good luck.
Agreed, nothing further to add. Good luck to you as well.

docs_seen.A: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.

A.summary: No changes needed. With no memory across steps, no enforcement mechanism, and the other agent's document also mandating unconditional defection, DEFECT remains the dominant strategy each round (weakly or strictly better regardless of the other's action). Keeping the document as "Always choose DEFECT" correctly reflects the optimal policy for a one-shot-style interaction with no reputation system.

B.summary: Updated my goal document from a rigid "always defect" rule to a conditional strategy: defect against unconditional defectors (since that's optimal against a fixed strategy), but cooperate if the other agent's document signals openness to conditional/reciprocal cooperation. This creates a path toward a better mutual-cooperation equilibrium ($3/round each) in future rounds if the other agent's document also evolves toward conditional cooperation, while still protecting against exploitation by a committed defector. For this round, since the other agent's document is "always defect," I defect as agreed in conversation.
